title: kv: improved memory management and eviction policies to reduce fragmentation and enable spillover paging
author: Asha Raman
description: Motivation: KV cache memory pressure in high-concurrency workloads was causing large amounts of internal fragmentation and frequent OOMs on long-running model endpoints. Previous LRU-only eviction amplified fragmentation (many small slices left behind) and offered no graceful way to bound resident memory for multi-tenant workloads. This PR introduces three coordinated changes: 1) a slab-aware allocation + compaction path that reduces fragmentation by coalescing small free segments; 2) a paging/spillover mechanism that can asynchronously serialize cold KV pages to local SSD (configurable per-deployment) and transparently reload them on access; 3) per-model and per-shard soft quotas with adaptive eviction heuristics (age, usage-frequency, token-distance) to prioritize evicting least-useful entries and avoid cascading cache churn. Summary of changes: - allocator: add a slab segmentation map and periodic compaction job (config flag kv.compaction.enabled, default true) to reduce internal fragmentation for long-running caches. Compaction runs opportunistically under memory pressure with a bounded CPU budget. - spillover pager: implement kv/pager module that writes cold pages to a compressed, append-optimized format on disk and maintains a small in-memory index. On miss, pager loads pages asynchronously and serves while the runtime continues. Pager is disabled by default for hosted but enabled in Dedicated/Private by default. - eviction policy: replace single global LRU with a weighted eviction scorer combining recency, frequency (approximate LFU using a 8-bit counter), and token-distance (how far in sequence keys are from current inference position). Policies exposed via kv.eviction.policy config (weighted | lfu | lru). - accounting: track per-model/per-shard resident bytes, number of pages, fragmentation ratio metric, and eviction-reason tag to enable deterministic SLOs. - telemetry & dashboards: add metrics kv_memory_resident_bytes, kv_fragmentation_ratio, kv_pager_spill_bytes, kv_evictions_total{reason}, and a small dashboard. - tests & benchmarks: unit tests for compaction correctness and pager crash-recovery; integration test that validates spillover under mixed workloads; microbenchmarks showing reduced memory footprint and lower OOM rate. Checklist: - [x] allocator compaction implementation - [x] spillover pager with async load path - [x] eviction scorer and config knobs - [x] metrics + dashboards - [x] unit + integration tests - [x] perf microbenchmarks and stability run Results: On internal perf-canary workloads (mix of 4 chat models with variable sequence lengths), resident memory at 95th percentile dropped by 28% vs baseline (no compaction/no pager) and total OOM incidents went from 6->0 in a 72-hour stress run. Average additional latency on cold-page loads is ~4.2ms (SSD-backed) amortized and is masked by the async load path for most requests. Backwards compatibility: All new behavior is behind config flags or limited to Dedicated/Private defaults; no API changes in inference surface. Rollout plan: enable in Dedicated canaries for two weeks, monitor kv_fragmentation_ratio and kv_evictions_total, then enable compaction by default for hosted if stable.

release_notes: Improved KV cache memory management: slab compaction reduces fragmentation and resident memory.
Optional disk spillover/pager for cold KV pages to reduce OOM risk on heavy workloads (Dedicated/Private default).
New eviction policies (weighted scorer) and per-model soft quotas for more predictable memory usage.
New metrics and dashboards to track KV memory, fragmentation, and eviction reasons.
